Effect of +def truncation on separable prior

  • Set simulation parameters
  • Simulate from prior
  • Format simulation output
  • Visualize results
    • Prior distribution on the number of edges
    • Edge probabilities
    • Diagonal entries
    • Off-diagonal entries
library(modelSelection)
library(tidyverse)
library(lamW)      # Lambert's W_q function
library(extraDistr)# Beta-Binomial distribution
set.seed(20260606) # for reproducibility
save2pdf <- TRUE  # set to true to write plots to pdf

Set simulation parameters

We consider a problem dimensions \(k=5\) and four prior edge inclusion probabilities \(P(Z_{ij}=1)= \eta \in \{ 0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4 \}\). We also consider a Beta-Binomial(1,2) prior where \(\eta \sim \mbox{Beta}(1,2)\) is random (with expectation \(E(\eta)=1/3\)), which implies a Beta-Binomial(1,2) distribution on the model size \(\sum_{i<j} Z_{ij}\). Non-zero off-diagonal entries are simulated \(\Theta_{ij} \mid Z_{ij}=1 \sim N(0, \sigma^2)\) where \(\sigma^2=1\), and \(Z_{ij}= \mbox{I}(\Theta_{ij} \neq 0)\) is an edge inclusion indicator for \(i > j\). Diagonal entries are generated \(\Theta_{ii} \sim \mbox{Exp}(\lambda / 2)\), where \(\lambda / 2\) is the rate parameter and hence \(2/\lambda\) the mean. As a first possible choice we consider \(\lambda = 1\).

kseq <- 50  # to consider more values of k let kseq be a vector, the code below remains valid
edge_prob_seq <- c(0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, -1)  # -1 signals Beta-Binomial prior
lambda1 <- 1

As a second possible choice for \(\lambda\), we set \(\lambda\) such that \(P(\Theta_{ii} \succ 0 \mid Z) \geq 1 - \alpha\), for every edge configuration \(Z\), taking \(\alpha=0.1\). Using the formulae given in the main paper, this is given by taking \[ \frac{2}{\lambda} > \frac{2 \sigma p \sqrt{\bar d}}{\alpha} \sqrt{- W_{-1}\left( \frac{-\alpha^2}{32 e^2 p^2} \right)}, \] where \(W_{-1}\) is the branch of Lambert’s \(W_q\) function associated to \(q=-1\), and setting \(\bar d= p\) as an upper-bound on the maximum edge degree. Note that this rule gives a value of \(\lambda\) that depends on \(p\), here for simplicity we take the \(\lambda\) value associated to the larger \(k=100\), since this also suffices for any \(p \leq 100\) (and the results remain virtually identical when using a different \(\lambda\) for \(k=5\)).

sd.slab <- 1
alpha <- 0.1
p <- max(kseq)
x <- - alpha^2 /(32 * exp(2) * p^2)
l <- lambertWm1(x) # q = -1 branch of Lambert's W_q function
mu <- (2 * sd.slab * p^(3/2) / alpha) * sqrt(-l) # conservative upper-bound
lambda2 <- 2/mu
lambda2
## [1] 6.181495e-05

Simulate from prior

fit1 <- fit2 <- lapply(1:length(kseq), function(z) vector("list", length(edge_prob_seq)))
priorCoef <- normalidprior(sd.slab^2)
for (i in 1:length(kseq)) {
  p <- kseq[i]
  y <- matrix(nrow=0, ncol=p)
  for (j in 1:length(edge_prob_seq)) {
    if (edge_prob_seq[j] >= 0) {
      priorModel <- modelbinomprior(edge_prob_seq[j])
      niter <- 5000
    } else {
      priorModel <- modelbbprior(1,2)
      niter <- 50000 #requires more iterations to converge
    }

    fit1[[i]][[j]] <- modelSelectionGGM(y, niter=niter, burnin=0, priorCoef=priorCoef, priorModel=priorModel, 
                                        priorDiag= exponentialprior(lambda1), verbose=FALSE)
    fit2[[i]][[j]] <- modelSelectionGGM(y, niter=niter, burnin=0, priorCoef=priorCoef, priorModel=priorModel, 
                                        priorDiag= exponentialprior(lambda2), verbose=FALSE)
    cat('.')
  }
  cat('\n')
}
## .....

Assess MCMC convergence.

par(mar= c(5,5,0.1,0.1), mfrow=c(2,1))
for (i in 1:length(kseq)) {
  for (j in 1:length(edge_prob_seq)) {
    plot(fit1[[i]][[j]]) 
    text(5000, 0.95, paste('k=', kseq[i], sep=''), pos=4)
    text(5000, 0.80, paste('edge_prob=', edge_prob_seq[j], sep=''), pos=4)
    text(5000, 0.65, paste('lambda=', lambda1, sep=''), pos=4)
    plot(fit2[[i]][[j]])
    text(5000, 0.95, paste('k=', kseq[i], sep=''), pos=4)
    text(5000, 0.80, paste('edge_prob=', edge_prob_seq[j], sep=''), pos=4)
    text(5000, 0.65, paste('lambda=', lambda2, sep=''), pos=4)
  }
}

Format simulation output

Store off-diagonal samples in a vector, discarding the burnin.

burnin <- 1000

empty_named_list <- function(z, element_names) {
  ans <- vector("list", length(edge_prob_seq))
  names(ans) <- element_names
  return(ans)
}

element_names <- paste("edge_prob = ", edge_prob_seq, sep='')
diagsamples1 <- lapply(1:length(kseq), empty_named_list, element_names=element_names)
names(diagsamples1) <- paste("k = ", kseq, sep='')
diagsamples2 <- offdiagsamples1 <- offdiagsamples2 <- total_edges1 <- total_edges2 <- diagsamples1


for (i in 1:length(kseq)) {
  for (j in 1:length(edge_prob_seq)) {
    diagentry <- fit1[[i]][[j]]$indexes[1,] == fit1[[i]][[j]]$indexes[2,]
    diagsamples1[[i]][[j]] <- as.vector(fit1[[i]][[j]]$postSample[-1:-burnin,diagentry])
    diagsamples2[[i]][[j]] <- as.vector(fit2[[i]][[j]]$postSample[-1:-burnin,diagentry])
    offdiagsamples1[[i]][[j]] <- as.vector(fit1[[i]][[j]]$postSample[-1:-burnin,!diagentry])
    offdiagsamples2[[i]][[j]] <- as.vector(fit2[[i]][[j]]$postSample[-1:-burnin,!diagentry])
    total_edges1[[i]][[j]] <- rowSums(as.matrix(fit1[[i]][[j]]$postSample[-1:-burnin,!diagentry] != 0))
    total_edges2[[i]][[j]] <- rowSums(as.matrix(fit2[[i]][[j]]$postSample[-1:-burnin,!diagentry] != 0))
  }
}

For each \(k\) and edge probability, we calculate the prior edge probability after truncation, standard deviation of non-zero off-diagonal entries, and mean diagonal entry.

pars <- expand.grid(k=factor(kseq), edge_prob=edge_prob_seq)

edge_prob_trunc <- sd_offdiag <- mean_diag <- matrix(NA, nrow=nrow(pars), ncol=2)
colnames(edge_prob_trunc) <- paste("lambda=",round(c(lambda1,lambda2),5))
colnames(sd_offdiag) <- colnames(mean_diag) <- colnames(edge_prob_trunc)
sd_nonzero <- function(x) sd(x[x != 0])
for (i in 1:nrow(pars)) {
  k <- pars$k[i]
  edge_prob <- pars$edge_prob[i]
  
  sel1 <- which(names(diagsamples1) == paste('k = ', k, sep=''))
  sel2 <- which(names(diagsamples1[[1]]) == paste('edge_prob = ', edge_prob, sep=''))
  
  edge_prob_trunc[i,1] <- mean(offdiagsamples1[[sel1]][[sel2]] != 0) 
  edge_prob_trunc[i,2] <- mean(offdiagsamples2[[sel1]][[sel2]] != 0) 
  sd_offdiag[i, 1] <- sd_nonzero(offdiagsamples1[[sel1]][[sel2]])
  sd_offdiag[i, 2] <- sd_nonzero(offdiagsamples2[[sel1]][[sel2]])
  mean_diag[i, 1] <- mean(diagsamples1[[sel1]][[sel2]])
  mean_diag[i, 2] <- mean(diagsamples2[[sel1]][[sel2]])
}
edge_prob_trunc <- cbind(pars, edge_prob_trunc) |>
  pivot_longer(cols=3:4, names_to="lambda") |>
  mutate(value = round(value, 3)) |>
  rename(edge_prob_trunc = value) |>
  mutate(lambda = factor(lambda)) |>
  mutate(lambda = factor(lambda, levels=rev(levels(lambda))))

sd_offdiag <- cbind(pars, sd_offdiag) |>
  pivot_longer(cols=3:4, names_to="lambda") |>
  mutate(value = round(value, 3)) |>
  rename(sd_offdiag = value) |>
  mutate(lambda = factor(lambda)) |>
  mutate(lambda = factor(lambda, levels=rev(levels(lambda))))

mean_diag <- cbind(pars, mean_diag) |>
  pivot_longer(cols=3:4, names_to="lambda") |>
  mutate(value = round(value, 3)) |>
  rename(mean_diag = value) |>
  mutate(lambda = factor(lambda)) |>
  mutate(lambda = factor(lambda, levels=rev(levels(lambda))))

We also obtain the prior distribution of the number of edges \(\sum_{i<j} Z_{ij}\), before and after truncation. The latter is estimated from MCMC output. For \(Z_{ij} \sim \mbox{Bern}(\eta)\), the former is given by a Binomial distribution with \(p(p-1)/2\) trials and success probability \(\eta\).

nedges1 <- nedges2 <- vector("list", length(total_edges1))
for (i in 1:length(total_edges1)) {
  totaledges <- as.integer(unlist(total_edges1[[i]]))
  lab <- rep(names(total_edges1[[i]]), sapply(total_edges1[[i]], length))
  nedges1[[i]] <- data.frame(nedges = totaledges, edge_prob = lab)
  #
  totaledges <- as.integer(unlist(total_edges2[[i]]))
  lab <- rep(names(total_edges2[[i]]), sapply(total_edges2[[i]], length))
  nedges2[[i]] <- data.frame(nedges = totaledges, edge_prob = lab)
}

nedges1 <- do.call(rbind, nedges1) |>
  mutate(k= rep(kseq, sapply(nedges1, nrow)))

nedges2 <- do.call(rbind, nedges2) |>
  mutate(k= rep(kseq, sapply(nedges2, nrow)))

We only evaluate the Binomial and Beta-Binomial priors for the largest \(k\), since we will restrict the later plot to such \(k\).

totaledges <- max(kseq) * (max(kseq)-1) / 2
nedges_binom <- vector("list", length(edge_prob_seq))
for (j in 1:length(edge_prob_seq)) {

  if (edge_prob_seq[j] >= 0) {
    pmf_edges <- dbinom(x=0:totaledges, size=totaledges, prob=edge_prob_seq[j])
  } else {
    pmf_edges <- dbbinom(0:totaledges, size=totaledges, alpha=1, beta=2)
  }
  number_edges <- rep(0:totaledges, round(50000 * pmf_edges, 4))
  
  nedges_binom[[j]] <- data.frame(edge_prob=edge_prob_seq[j],
                                  number_edges = number_edges) |>
                       mutate(trunc = "Before truncation")
  
}
nedges_binom <- do.call(rbind, nedges_binom)

Prior distribution on the number of edges

We plot the prior distribution on the number of edges under \(\lambda=1\), for a prior edge probability of 0.05 and for the Beta-Binomial model prior.

data2plot <- filter(nedges1, k==max(kseq)) |>
  mutate(edge_prob = sub("edge_prob = ", "", edge_prob)) |>
  mutate(edge_prob = as.numeric(edge_prob), trunc = "After truncation") |>
  select(edge_prob, nedges, trunc) |>
  rename(number_edges = nedges) |>
  rbind(nedges_binom) |>
  mutate(edge_prob = paste("Edge probability = ", edge_prob, sep=''))
filter(data2plot, edge_prob == "Edge probability = 0.05") |>
ggplot(aes(x=number_edges, col=trunc)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), fill=NA, position="identity") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.85), legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_grey() +
  xlab("Number of edges") +
  ylab("Prior probability")
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

if (save2pdf) ggsave("prior_number_edges_edgeprob05.pdf")
## Saving 7 x 5 in image
## `stat_bin()` using `bins = 30`. Pick better value `binwidth`.

ggplot(aes(x=number_edges, col=trunc)) +

  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.8, 0.85), legend.title = element_blank()) +
  scale_color_grey() +

Edge probabilities

We plot the edge inclusion probabilities before and after truncation. For the Beta-Binomial(1,1), the marginal prior edge inclusion probability is 1/3.

mutate(edge_prob_trunc, edge_prob= ifelse(edge_prob >= 0, edge_prob, 1/3)) |>
ggplot(aes(x=edge_prob, y=edge_prob_trunc, col=k)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_abline(lty=2) +
  facet_wrap(~ lambda) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 15) +
  theme(legend.position = c(0.1, 0.85)) +
  scale_color_grey() +
  xlab("Edge probability (before truncation)") +
  ylab("Edge probability (after truncation)")

if (save2pdf) ggsave("prior_edge_prob.pdf")
## Saving 7 x 5 in image

Diagonal entries

Plot density before and after positive-definiteness truncation. First, for diagonal entries. We create a function that obtains a kernel density estimate, via taking a log transformation of the input and then performing the associated change of variables.

log_density <- function(x, threshold=0.1, ...) {
  if (any(x <= 0, na.rm = TRUE)) stop("All values of x must be > 0")

  y <- log(x)
  dens_y <- density(y, ...)
  x_grid <- exp(dens_y$x)
  
  sel <- (x_grid > threshold)
  x_grid <- x_grid[sel] # avoid numerical instability close to 0
  f_x <- dens_y$y[sel] / x_grid   # apply Jacobian term (divide by x)

  ans <- list(x = x_grid, y = f_x, bw = dens_y$bw, n = dens_y$n, call = match.call(),
      data.name = deparse(substitute(x)), has.na = dens_y$has.na)
  structure(ans, class = "density") # return a 'density' object
}
col <- c('gray', rep('black', length(kseq)))
lwd <- c(3,rep(1,length(kseq)))
lty <- c(1, 1:length(kseq))
for (j in 1:length(edge_prob_seq)) {

  edge_prob <- edge_prob_seq[j]
  ylab <- paste('Prior density (edge prob=', edge_prob,')',sep='')
  if (length(kseq) > 1) {
    lab <- c('Before truncation', paste('After truncation (k=', kseq, ')',sep=''))
  } else {
    lab <- c('Before truncation', 'After truncation')
  }

  # Plot for lambda = 1
  dseq <- seq(0.01, max(diagsamples1[[1]][[j]]), length=200)
  if (edge_prob_seq[j] >= 0) {
    fname <- paste("priordiag_edgeprob_", edge_prob_seq[j], "_lambda1.pdf", sep='')
  } else {
    fname <- paste("priordiag_bbin_lambda1.pdf", sep='')
  }
  if (save2pdf) pdf(fname)
  par(mar= c(5,5,0.1,0.1), cex.lab=1.5, cex.axis=1.5, mfrow=c(1,1))

  plot(dseq, dexp(dseq, rate=lambda1/2), xlab="Diagonal entry", ylab=ylab, 
       type='l', col=col[1], lwd=lwd[1], lty=lty[1])
  for (i in 1:length(kseq)) {
    lines(log_density(diagsamples1[[i]][[j]]), col=col[i+1], lty=lty[i+1], lwd=lwd[i+1])
  }
  
  legend('topright', lab, col= col, lwd=lwd, lty=lty, cex=1.3)

  if (save2pdf) dev.off()

  # Plot for smaller lambda
  dseq <- seq(0.01, qexp(0.99, rate=lambda2/2), length=200)
  if (edge_prob_seq[j] >= 0) {
    fname <- paste("priordiag_edgeprob_", edge_prob_seq[j], "_lambda2.pdf", sep='')
  } else {
    fname <- paste("priordiag_edgeprob_bbin_lambda2.pdf", sep='')
  }
  if (save2pdf) pdf(fname)
  par(mar= c(5,5,0.1,0.1), cex.lab=1.5, cex.axis=1.5, mfrow=c(1,1))

  plot(dseq, dexp(dseq, rate=lambda2/2), xlab="Diagonal entry", ylab=ylab, 
       type='l', col=col[1], lwd=lwd[1], lty=lty[1])
  for (i in 1:length(kseq)) {
    lines(log_density(diagsamples2[[i]][[j]]), col=col[i+1], lty=lty[i+1], lwd=lwd[i+1])
  }
  
  legend('topright', lab, col= col, lwd=lwd, lty=lty, cex=1.3)

  if (save2pdf) dev.off()

}

Off-diagonal entries

Finally, we plot the marginal densities of the off-diagonal entries.

col <- c('gray', rep('black', length(kseq)))
lwd <- c(3,rep(1,length(kseq)))
lty <- c(1, 1:length(kseq))
for (j in 1:length(edge_prob_seq)) {

  edge_prob <- edge_prob_seq[j]
  ylab <- paste('Prior density (edge prob=', edge_prob,')',sep='')
  if (length(kseq) > 1) {
    lab <- c('Before truncation', paste('After truncation (k=', kseq, ')',sep=''))
  } else {
    lab <- c('Before truncation', 'After truncation')
  }
  oseq <- seq(-3.5, 3.5, length=200)

  # Plot for lambda = 1
  if (edge_prob_seq[j] >= 0) {
    fname <- paste("prioroffdiag_edgeprob_", edge_prob_seq[j], "_lambda1.pdf", sep='')
  } else {
    fname <- paste("prioroffdiag_bbin_lambda1.pdf", sep='')
  }
  if (save2pdf) pdf(fname)
  par(mar= c(5,5,0.1,0.1), cex.lab=1.5, cex.axis=1.5, mfrow=c(1,1))

  dnorm_oseq <- dnorm(oseq, sd=1)
  ylim <- c(0, 1.5*max(dnorm_oseq))
  plot(oseq, dnorm_oseq, xlab="Off-diagonal entry", ylab=ylab, 
       type='l', col=col[1], lwd=lwd[1], lty=lty[1], ylim=ylim)
  for (i in 1:length(kseq)) {
    nonzeroes <- offdiagsamples1[[i]][[j]]
    nonzeroes <- nonzeroes[nonzeroes != 0]
    lines(density(nonzeroes), col=col[i+1], lty=lty[i+1], lwd=lwd[i+1])
  }
  
  legend('topright', lab, col= col, lwd=lwd, lty=lty, cex=1.2)

  if (save2pdf) dev.off()

  # Plot for smaller lambda
  if (edge_prob_seq[j] >= 0) {
    fname <- paste("prioroffdiag_edgeprob_", edge_prob_seq[j], "_lambda2.pdf", sep='')
  } else {
    fname <- paste("prioroffdiag_bbin_lambda2.pdf", sep='')
  }
  if (save2pdf) pdf(fname)
  par(mar= c(5,5,0.1,0.1), cex.lab=1.5, cex.axis=1.5, mfrow=c(1,1))

  plot(oseq, dnorm(oseq, sd=1), xlab="Off-diagonal entry", ylab=ylab, 
       type='l', col=col[1], lwd=lwd[1], lty=lty[1], ylim=ylim)
  for (i in 1:length(kseq)) {
    nonzeroes <- offdiagsamples2[[i]][[j]]
    nonzeroes <- nonzeroes[nonzeroes != 0]
    lines(density(nonzeroes), col=col[i+1], lty=lty[i+1], lwd=lwd[i+1])
  }
  
  legend('topright', lab, col= col, lwd=lwd, lty=lty, cex=1.2)

  if (save2pdf) dev.off()

}
